newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-France poll worry takes toll of Euro bourses.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France poll worry takes toll of Euro bourses.

text.p: Europe's major stock markets all suffered on Wednesday, but French shares were hammered by investor worries that the opposition Socialists may be well placed for Sunday's runoff parliamentary elections.

The French rout, which saw the blue chip CAC-40 index lose 4.4 percent of its value at one point, came after rumours swept the market about privately commissioned polls predicting the likely outcome of the National Assembly elections.
The market picked itself off the floor during the afternoon but still closed with a loss of 97.17 points, or 3.63 percent, at 2,583.17 for the second big fall of the week.
Several European stock markets bubbled to fresh trading highs during the morning, but a combination of weakening bond markets, French worries and a negative start on Wall Street damaged sentiment.
Nerves over the French election and its possible impact on European economic and monetary union weighed on the dollar in late European trade.
The franc also fell to a near four-month low against the mark of 3.3828 before edging back slightly.
The French stock market provided the main drama, however, with the CAC-40 falling the most in percentage terms in four years before struggling off its lows.
The CAC index lost 3.91 percent on Monday, then rebounded nearly one percent on Tuesday before poll rumours triggered the fresh selloff on Wednesday in very heavy turnover of 12.45 billion francs.
One French trader said the market was being bombarded by rumours about private polls on the elections, but the findings could not be divulged under French law before the runoff vote on Sunday.
"There are significant market concerns over the prospect of the Socialists winning the election," Mike Young, director of European investment strategy at Goldman Sachs in London.
Although several European stock markets pushed their way into record territory during the morning, the good times could not last.
Germany's 30-share DAX index hit a trading high of 3,632.33 in early trade but went into retreat after failing to penetrate the psychologically important 3,700-point level.
The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade down 37.94 points at 3,636.42. In later screen-based trade, the IBIS DAX ended down 38.83 points at 3,626.60 ahead of a holiday on Thursday.
Traders said the holiday and nervousness about the French election made them reluctant to take fresh positions.
London investors were also cheered initially by Wall Street's strong performance on Tuesday, but went into a decline as events in France took their toll.
The FTSE 100 index closed with a loss of just 4.1 points at 4,677.5 as the Dow Industrial Average recovered to show a modest gain of about five points as European markets closed.

Dealers noted fears that a French coalition of Socialist and Communists, which won the first-round ballot last Sunday, could scrap an austerity drive to qualify for Europe's monetary union if they won on Sunday.
Shares in Guinness Plc and Grand Metropolitan Plc led FTSE 100 decliners, each shedding more than two percent after news that LVMH intended to buy all Guinness' interest in their joint ventures.
Platinum and palladium prices also soared to fresh highs during the day on news of a strike at Anglo American Platinum Corp's Rustenburg mine in South Africa.
Palladium was fixed in London at a record $188.00 in the morning but slipped back to $186 at the afternoon fix.
CURRENCIES AT 1600 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6940 marks and 115.53 yen compared with 1.7045 marks and 116.50 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING INDICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed down 4.1 points, or 0.09 percent, at 4,677.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed down 97.17 points, or 3.63 percent, at 2,583.17.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade down 37.94 points, or 1.03 percent, at 3,636.50. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX ended down 38.83 points, or 1.06 percent, at 3,626.6.
PRECIOUS METALS
Palladium closed up $20.25 at $196.50, while platinum ended firmer, up $4.60 at $401.60. Gold closed at $345.05 up $1.30, while silver was three cents easier at $4.72.
